text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's unemployment rate was 13 percent in March, showing a 0.4 percent decline compared with February, and proved the best result in five years, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
In March last year unemployment was 15.4 percent.
- Warsaw provincial governor Bohdan Jastrzebski has closed down the soccer stadiums of Legia Warszawa and Polonia Warszawa soccer clubs as a consequence of hooligan riots at a match on Sunday.
The stadiums will be allowed to reopen when they fulfill security conditions set out by the city security commission.
- Poland's newest SW-4 PZL helicopter will be shown at France's Le Bourget aircraft industry exhibition in June.
The new chopper's loading capacity is 400 kg, average cruising speed is 240 km and maximum flying range 900 km.

- Around 800 former Gdansk shipyard workers will be contracted to complete construction of the B-683 bulk carrier, which was under construction when the yard went bankrupt, the yard's deputy director Bogdan Oleszek said.
- A Polish Italian joint venture, Tino's, has bought the FRiOS leather garment plant in Miastko, Slupsk province, for 800,000 zlotys.
Tino's guaranteed to invest $90,000 in facility modernisation and development in the next two years and to employ the plant's 300 workers for at least one year.
The plant was burdened with debts of nine million zlotys.

- Two Russian fishing trawlers contracted to fish for herring and sprat by Poland's Korab and Kuter fishing firms were arrested by Polish sea-border patrol for fishing in Poland's 12-mile border zone.
The ships were soon set free and assigned a fishing zone as the two ailing companies which contracted them could not afford the expensive services offered by Polish fishermen.
- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.5 percent this year, a recent report by the Salomon Brothers investment bank said.
- Port Gdynia Holding's net profit was 22.3 million zlotys in 1996, when the port reloaded 8.5 million tonnes of cargo.

- The general shareholders meeting of Polish Investment Bank (PBI), recently taken over by Kredyt Bank, has dismissed four former board members: Witold Kozinski, Zbigniew Lewandowski, Krzysztof Imielowski, and Grzegorz Gorski, and elected new members including Stanislaw Pacuk, Dariusz Sokolowski, Malgorzata Krokier-Jachiewicz and Witold Sowilski.

- Austria's Creditanstalt Financial Advisers (CAFA) is planning to act as the privatisation adviser of the Nafta Polska petrol distribution holding and participate in the consolidation of Poland's food processing sector.
- Bank Wlasnosci Pracowniczej (BWP) hopes to raise $1 million through a C-series share issue this month, the bank's president Kazimierz Glowacki said.
- Poland's oil proccessing sector needs up to $5.8 billion for modernisation and development, some sector experts said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's unemployment is likely to fall below 12 percent in mid-1997, Poland's Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said.
- The Nafta Polska oil holding has received 17 tender offers produced by consulting firms interested in advising the holding's privatisation.

- Mostostal Zabrze has proposed to act as the main constructor of the Isuzu and Delphi factories to be built in the Katowice special economic zone in southern Poland, Mostostal's spokesman Piotr Grabowski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's Telimena and Emfor garment makers will form a holding in the next two years to become the country's seventh biggest garment maker, Telimena's president Tadeusz Wawrzyniak said.
ZYCIE
- Austrian bank Creditanstalt is mulling the purchase of the Pekao SA banking group to be privatised in 1998, Creditanstalt Financial Advisers SA board member Jerzy Gumowski said.
PARKIET
- The Nowe Zycie Gospodarcze economic weekly is planning a share listing on the Warsaw bourse by the end of 1998.
